science.title: Attentive temporal patch filtering for explainable streaming intrusion detection in medical IoT traffic
science.description: Network traffic in the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) forms an unbounded multivariate temporal sequence whose statistics shift across devices, protocols, and acquisition environments; detecting malicious segments within it is a streaming time-series classification problem constrained by bounded per-window latency, essential for temporally localized explanations, and robustness to distribution shift. This research work presents TAPX-Net, a window-local classifier that decomposes each traffic window into temporal patches, applies channel-attentive depthwise convolutional filtering, and models the patch sequence with stacked bidirectional recurrent layers before attention pooling and dual classification and reconstruction heads. Each window is classified independently, with recurrent states reset at every window boundary, making the model window-causal. A temporal attribution module (TAM) produces patch- and feature-level explanations through Integrated Gradients (IG), validated against a causal input-level ablation. A feature-harmonized adaptation stage transfers the trained model to new network environments through limited-label fine-tuning with Maximum Mean Discrepancy alignment. On the CICIoMT2024 benchmark, TAPX-Net reaches a recall of 0.9541 at an FPR of one percent and a zero-day recall of 0.8963 across ten held-out attack classes, exceeding 7 baselines on every detection metric, and under CPU-only inference on the tested configuration processes a continuous stream at 108.7 windows per second with 98.8 percent of decisions within a 10 ms per-window bound. IG tracks the causal ablation more closely than attention weights (AW) across all attack classes, and cross-dataset transfer (CDT) to the general-purpose UNSW-NB15 and ToN-IoT benchmarks recovers most of the achievable performance gain with 5,000 labeled target windows. The reconstruction head contributes a 7.46 percentage point improvement in zero-day recall, focused on the generalization regime.

science.title: Live-cell 3D mapping reveals the organized architecture of FG-nucleoporins within the nuclear pore complex
science.description: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) governs selective nucleocytoplasmic exchange, yet the spatial organization of its intrinsically disordered FG nucleoporins (FG-Nups) in living cells has remained unresolved. Here we reconstruct the three-dimensional distributions of all eleven mammalian FG-Nups within individual NPCs in live cells by combining high-speed 2D single-molecule tracking with post-localization 2D-to-3D transformation, validated by Monte Carlo simulations and independent 3D MINFLUX measurements. The resulting map reveals that the FG barrier is not a uniform disordered meshwork but a stratified architecture. Five centrally anchored FG-Nups form an annular structure surrounding a sparsely occupied axial corridor, whereas six asymmetrically positioned FG-Nups extend flexibly beyond the scaffold to generate dynamic caps at the cytoplasmic and nucleoplasmic faces. Nup214 and Nup153 switch between open and closed axial conformations, whereas Nup98 spans nearly the full pore length and overlaps with most other FG-Nups, linking the major FG zones across the barrier. Together, these features define an adaptable capped channel extending up to ~270 nm across the nuclear envelope, with a ~ 40 nm annular central region and FG extensions reaching ~80–130 nm into the cytoplasm and ~60–100 nm into the nucleoplasm. Transport-route measurements in the same live-cell system show that passive diffusion preferentially traverses the relatively FG-poor central corridor, whereas facilitated transport follows peripheral FG-rich pathways. These findings provide a unified structural framework for NPC selectivity and support a model in which distributed, position-dependent FG architectures, rather than a single central barrier, organize transport. 3D imaging in living cells reveals how nuclear pore FG-Nups organize: five central FG-Nups form a ring around a sparse axial corridor, while six asymmetric FG-Nups form dynamic caps, together directing diffusion and selective transport.

science.title: Plasma-treated porous carriers for modulating clove essential oil release against Tropilaelaps mites in Apis mellifera colonies
science.description: Tropilaelaps mites are among the most destructive ectoparasites of Apis mellifera. The application of essential oil-based acaricides to control their populations is limited by rapid volatilization and short persistence under hive conditions. This study investigated pumice and ceramic balls treated with argon or helium non-thermal atmospheric pressure plasma (NTAPP), with or without water vapor, to modify the evaporation profile of clove essential oil for Tropilaelaps mite control. Plasma treatment did not significantly affect clove essential oil adsorption capacity (0.0072–0.0092 μL mg−1 and 0.0049–0.0065 μL mg−1 for pumice and ceramic balls, respectively). However, the He + H2O-treated ceramic ball exhibited significantly slower evaporation during days 2–8, although all treatments reached approximately 52–54% cumulative evaporation after 14 days. In laboratory bioassays using 5% clove essential oil, mite mortality differed between plasma-treated and untreated ceramic balls during the initial 30 min of exposure for the 0 and 24 h evaporation periods. However, both treatments resulted in 100% mite mortality after 3 h of exposure across all evaporation periods (0, 6, and 24 h). Adult bee survival was comparable between the two treatments but differed from the control. During the 28-day field trial, colonies treated with 5% clove essential oil-loaded ceramic balls showed numerically lower mite infestation than those treated with formic acid, with comparable adult bee populations and no significant differences among treatments. Overall, plasma surface modification modulated the evaporation profile of clove essential oil without compromising its acaricidal activity, supporting the potential use of plasma-treated porous carriers as delivery systems for Tropilaelaps mite management.

science.title: Multicenter evaluation of AI-based intraocular lens formulas and interpretable machine learning for cataract refractive prediction
science.description: Accurate intraocular lens (IOL) power selection remains challenging in cataract eyes with long axial length, altered corneal geometry, or previous corneal refractive surgery. This multicenter retrospective study evaluated conventional, post-refractive, and AI-based IOL formulas and developed interpretable machine learning models for postoperative refractive prediction. The development cohort included 1203 eyes from West China Hospital; the external validation cohort included 336 high-myopia eyes from Chengdu Aidi Eye Hospital, with 257 eyes available for cleaned counterfactual target-achievement analysis. Formula and model performance were assessed using mean absolute error, root mean square error, median absolute error, and predefined refractive error thresholds. In eyes without prior corneal refractive surgery, AI-based formulas outperformed conventional formulas, with Hill-RBF showing the lowest internal prediction error. Locally developed linear regression, support vector regression, and random forest models achieved comparable internal accuracy, but external validation showed reduced portability. SHAP analysis identified target refraction, axial length, and IOL power as dominant predictors. Post-refractive eyes, very long eyes, and flat corneas remained difficult. These findings support cautious, locally validated use of AI-based formulas and interpretable machine learning in refractive cataract surgery.

science.title: Empagliflozin does not rescue nor exacerbate doxorubicin-induced skeletal muscle wasting and metabolic dysfunction in male mice
science.description: Doxorubicin (DOX) can induce skeletal muscle and white adipose tissue (WAT) wasting, contributing to treatment-related body mass loss, functional decline and compromised treatment efficacy. Impaired protein turnover and energy metabolism have been proposed as contributing mechanisms. Sodium–glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) induce glucosuria and systemic metabolic adaptations that may improve skeletal muscle protein homeostasis and metabolic regulation. Concurrently, the glucosuria-induced caloric loss associated with SGLT2is may interfere with tissue wasting. This study investigated whether empagliflozin (EMPA) modifies DOX-induced tissue wasting in male mice. C57BL/6J mice (n = 36) were randomized to control, EMPA, DOX, or DOX-EMPA groups. DOX (4 mg/kg/week, intraperitoneally) and EMPA (10 mg/kg/day, oral gavage) were administered for 6-weeks. Whole-body energy metabolism was assessed by indirect calorimetry, followed by tissue weight and molecular analyses in skeletal muscle and WAT. EMPA neither attenuated nor exacerbated DOX-induced body weight, skeletal muscle, or WAT loss. Despite effective glucosuria, EMPA did not increase non-fasted circulating β-hydroxybutyrate levels or meaningfully modify DOX-associated alterations in whole-body energy metabolism, tissue wasting, molecular markers of skeletal muscle protein turnover and metabolic regulation, or metabolic and stress-related gene expression in WAT. In conclusion, EMPA did not protect against DOX-induced tissue wasting and associated metabolic dysfunction, nor did it aggravate these effects.

science.title: Causal-enhanced federated transfer learning framework for privacy-preserving cross-organizational strategic collaboration
science.description: Cross-organizational strategic collaboration increasingly demands data-driven coordination while confronting stringent privacy constraints and heterogeneous data distributions. This paper proposes a coupled framework integrating causal inference with federated transfer learning to enable effective knowledge sharing across organizational boundaries without centralizing sensitive data. The framework comprises three core components: a distributed causal discovery algorithm that reconstructs inter-organizational causal structures through secure aggregation protocols, a causal-enhanced federated transfer learning mechanism that identifies invariant features transferable across heterogeneous enterprise contexts, and an adaptive privacy computing architecture that dynamically allocates protection resources according to data sensitivity profiles. Experimental validation across multi-enterprise ecosystems demonstrates that the causal enhancement mechanism improves cross-domain generalization robustness by 43% compared to conventional federated transfer learning, while maintaining predictive accuracy within 6.2% of centralized approaches. The adaptive privacy architecture retains 93.7% of collaborative utility under meaningful privacy constraints, with membership inference attack success rates near random baseline. These results establish that properly designed federated frameworks can approach centralized performance while preserving organizational autonomy, enabling broader participation in data-driven strategic alliances across regulatory and competitive boundaries.
